title: Bridging backpressure spiral - hosted API streaming outage digest
body:
Summary:

On 2026-05-19 between ~03:17 and ~04:02 UTC we observed a degradation across hosted API streaming endpoints affecting p95/p99 response times and causing elevated 5xx rates for streaming sessions. Impact: intermittent streaming stalls and ~13% of open streaming sessions saw early termination with 502/503 responses. Non-streaming generation endpoints were mildly affected (p50/p90 increase only).

What happened (high level):
A combination of: 1) a recent autoscaler policy change for edge acceptors that reduced ephemeral acceptor capacity under burst; 2) an assembly-layer "bridge" process that demultiplexes edge streams into internal muxed input queues which was recently rolled with a priority scheduler tweak; and 3) cross-region KV cache eviction spikes caused by a TTL mis-calculation — produced a backpressure amplification loop. The bridge prioritized small control frames over ongoing token streams, causing head-of-line stalls; stalled streams held KV cache leases and increased load on the serving pool, which triggered the autoscaler to oscillate and reduce acceptor capacity further, making the stalls worse.

Customer impact:
- 13% of streaming sessions in us-west and eu-central saw serial stalls or disconnects during the window.
- Several enterprise customers reported degraded UX for streaming chat (slow or truncated responses).
- No data loss of user messages recorded; reconnects recovered most sessions.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 03:17 Alert: streaming-session-error-rate increased past alert threshold (ops.streaming.session_errors > 0.7% for 5m)
- 03:22 Pager: on-call SRE paged for streaming errors & p99 latency spikes for /v1/stream responses
- 03:23 Initial triage: dashboards show concurrent kvcache evictions spike, edge acceptor queue length rising, bridge queue latencies diverging across zones
- 03:30 Hypothesis formed: recent autoscaler patch rolled to canary (edge-acceptor autoscaler v2.1.3) correlated with times of increased queueing
- 03:34 Mitigation 1: roll back autoscaler policy to v2.1.1 on canary and limit new canary propagation (Ethan)
- 03:38 Observed partial improvement in acceptor capacity but bridge latencies remained elevated due to KV pressure
- 03:42 Mitigation 2: emergency increase of acceptor backlog and ephemeral connection pool limits (Lena)
- 03:48 Mitigation 3: temporarily raised bridge worker count and disabled the new priority-scheduler flag (Marco)
- 03:55 p95 streaming latency trending back to baseline; 5xx rates falling but not fully recovered
- 04:02 Declared the incident contained; monitoring continued for 24h

Root cause analysis:
Primary root cause: priority inversion in the bridge demultiplexer combined with a brittle autoscaler policy. The bridge's new scheduling flag caused control frames (heartbeats and connection metadata) to be elevated in priority at the expense of active token-stream writes. This produced bursty stalls in long-lived streams.

Contributing factors:
- Autoscaler tuning assumed a stable headroom model; it responds to queue depth with aggressive scale-down when CPU appears low, which caused acceptor capacity to shrink during ephemeral bursts triggered by stalls.
- KV cache TTL mis-calculation: a code path that recalculates TTL on lease renewal used a fallback that shortened TTL during eviction storms, increasing cache misses and eviction churn across regions.
- Insufficient early telemetry: we lacked an alert that directly correlates per-session token stalls (byte gaps) to bridge queue position, so diagnosis required stitching multiple dashboards.

Why safeguards didn't prevent it:
- Canary scope was too broad: the autoscaler patch was allowed to run on ~8% of production acceptors and triggered systemic behavior because acceptors share upstream bridge resources.
- No automated preflight connecting streaming head-of-line tests for the bridge change.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back autoscaler change to previous stable version (v2.1.1) on canary and paused rollout
- Increased acceptor backlog and ephemeral limits on affected rings to reduce connection ejection
- Disabled new priority-scheduler flag in the bridge service and restarted workers to drain stuck queues
- Emergency KV TTL stabilization: forced TTL floor during eviction storms to reduce churn
- Applied tenant-level soft throttles for highest-traffic customers to reduce load while recovery progressed

Follow-up / long-term fixes (action items):
1) Bridge scheduler hardening (owner: Marco Alvarez, due 2026-06-09): revert fine-grained priority preemption; implement a fairness window that guarantees write forward progress for streams. Add unit + integration tests that simulate mixed control+token traffic.
2) Autoscaler hysteresis and safety limits (owner: Ethan Kim, due 2026-06-02): add minimum acceptor headroom floor, extend cooldown windows, prevent scale-downs below X% during transient queue spikes.
3) KV cache TTL audit & fix (owner: Priya Nambiar, due 2026-05-31): root-cause the TTL fallback bug, add regression tests, and add a monitored TTL floor metric.
4) New telemetry & alerts (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-05-28): add an alert that fires when token-gap-per-session > Y ms correlated with bridge queue position; instrument a bridge-end-to-end synthetic test and add preflight gate for bridge/acceptor rollouts.
5) Canary scope policy update (owner: SRE lead, due 2026-06-07): limit canary to non-critical rings and implement a cross-service blast radius scanner before rollout.
6) Runbook update (owner: Lena Fischer, due 2026-05-25): add a "bridge backpressure spiral" checklist and explicit mitigation steps (rollback autoscaler, disable scheduler flag, increase acceptor backlog, KV TTL floor).

Runbook changes (short):
- New alert: streaming.token-gap-correlated (severity: page)
- Immediate checklist for streaming stalls:
  * Check bridge queue latency by region
  * Check acceptor backlog and autoscaler recent decisions
  * If autoscaler changed within last 10m, halt rollout and rollback
  * If bridge scheduler flag present, disable and restart workers
  * If KV eviction rate > threshold, enable TTL floor

Post-incident metrics and queries to preserve:
- ops.streaming.session_errors / minute by region and tenant
- infra.bridge.queue_latency.p95/p99 by region
- infra.acceptor.scaler_actions (scale_in/scale_out events) with timestamps
- kvcache.eviction_rate and kvcache.ttl_distribution

Communications:
- Notified affected customers via CS incident channel with preliminary impact statement (CS ticket INF-2345).
- Internal incident summary posted to #SRE-oncall and ops-incident-runbook page.

Lessons learned:
- Even small scheduler priority tweaks can amplify into system-wide effects when multiple feedback loops exist. Test both isolated and integrated paths.
- Canary policies must consider shared downstream resources; a small percent of canary can still saturate shared bridges.
- Make the observability signal for "streaming head-of-line" explicit and actionable.

Appendix (artifacts and quick links):
- Grafana dashboard snapshots: grafana/d/streaming-session-health
- Relevant PR: serving-runtime PR #4127 (bridge scheduler tweak)
- Jira: INF-2345 (customer impact, tickets), INF-2360 (runbook updates), INF-2361 (autoscaler hysteresis)

Open action items (short list with owners):
- Marco: schedule integration tests for bridge fairness (due 2026-06-09)
- Ethan: implement autoscaler minimum headroom and cooldown (due 2026-06-02)
- Priya: fix TTL calculation and add regression (due 2026-05-31)
- Lena: update runbook and add the checklist to runbooks repo (due 2026-05-25)
- Aisha: ship synthetic bridge preflight and alert (due 2026-05-28)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working digest intended for SRE + infra + serving-runtime engineers. Please add any additional telemetry suggestions and proposed thresholds in comments below.

End of digest.
